documents.title: Outside ED Record Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
ED record from 11/16/25 finally received after the second fax request in December. 5 pages, attached. Routed to PCP.

PCP note 1/13: Reviewed. Food anaphylaxis after fruit salad, epi IM, 2 L saline, antihistamines, discharged after 6 h. Their allergy list matches what we updated in December. Filed.

documents.title: Eczema cream
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My hands are flaring with the cold and all the hand washing in lab. The triamcinolone is empty. Could I get a refill? Same as before.

documents.title: RE: Eczema cream
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Refill is in. Thin layer twice a day on the patches, and a thick fragrance-free moisturizer after every wash. If it isn't settling in two weeks, send me a photo.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is in her office on campus; identity checked by birth date.

Wants to get ahead of tree pollen season. Usual pattern is sneezing, itchy eyes and congestion through spring. No new reactions since November, no ED visits. Hands better after the cream.

Meds reviewed. Allergies reviewed: peanut, tree nuts, kiwi, banana, avocado.

Appears well on video, no conjunctival redness, speaking full sentences, no audible wheeze.

A/P:
- Allergic rhinitis: start fluticasone daily now through June; cetirizine as needed. Refills sent.
- Mild persistent asthma: albuterol refill sent.
- Peanut and food allergies: pens in date (checked the label on camera).
- Physical in early June.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 y/o here for her first physical with us.

Interval: no allergic reactions since the November ED visit. Allergy season was manageable on fluticasone and cetirizine. Eczema quiet since February. Asthma: albuterol as needed.

Meds: albuterol HFA prn; epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector x2; cetirizine 10 mg prn; fluticasone nasal in season; triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn.
Allergies: peanut (anaphylaxis), tree nuts, kiwi, banana, avocado (anaphylaxis to fruit salad 11/2025).
FH: mother allergic rhinitis and eczema; father asthma; brother peanut allergy.
SH: never smoker, 1-2 drinks/week.
Gyn: periods regular. Last Pap 2023 normal.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal, TMs clear, nasal mucosa unremarkable. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, no masses. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected. Skin without active eczema. Neuro grossly normal. Mood good. PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: Pap today. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, CBC, CMP and lipids drawn. Vaccines up to date (flu and COVID 10/2025, Tdap 2019, HPV complete).
- Peanut, tree nut and fruit allergies: pens in date, action plan reviewed again.
- Mild persistent asthma, allergic rhinitis, eczema: continue current meds.

RTC one year, sooner as needed. Results through the portal.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kayla, your blood work from Friday is all normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. The Pap usually takes about a week; I'll message when it's back.

documents.title: Pap Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pap is normal. Next one in three years.

events.reason: Trouble breathing, facial swelling and hives after cake

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital emergency department, 06/30/2026, triaged 19:55.

CC: difficulty breathing, facial swelling, generalized itchy rash after eating cake.

HPI: 27 y/o F, third ED presentation for suspected anaphylaxis after two episodes in 2025. At a friend's birthday party she had a piece of cake and about 30 min later developed the above. Concerned the cake was made with peanut oil. Background of eczema and allergic rhinitis, also mild persistent asthma.

Meds: albuterol HFA prn; epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg x2; cetirizine 10 mg prn; fluticasone nasal seasonal; triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn.
Allergies: peanut.
FHx: mother eczema/allergic rhinitis, father asthma, brother peanut allergy.
SHx: graduate student; never smoker; social alcohol 1-2/wk.

Arrival vitals: BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 25, SpO2 92% RA.

Exam: lips angioedematous. Urticaria across the trunk and both arms. Bilateral wheezes. Tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft. Alert, oriented.

ED course: epinephrine 0.3 mg IM given immediately on arrival. Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV, albuterol neb, normal saline 1 L IV. Lip swelling and hives improved over 2 hours, wheeze resolved, BP and HR normalized on recheck, saturation normal on room air. No biphasic symptoms during observation.
Labs: serum tryptase elevated. Total IgE elevated. CBC and BMP within normal limits.

Assessment: anaphylaxis, suspected peanut (peanut oil) exposure.

Disposition: home 01:20 on 7/1. Epinephrine auto-injector 2-pack prescribed. Strict peanut avoidance; follow up with PCP.

Emergency medicine physician.

documents.body: Pharmacy fill history shows an epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector 2-pack filled 7/1, prescribed by an ED provider at the community hospital on 6/30. No ED record or call from the patient yet. Release on file from the prior requests; ED record requested. Routed to PCP.
